title: Staging overrides leak into the prod config
statement:
We build per-environment configs from shared defaults with buildkit.config.merge_layers(). Building one environment changes the next one:

    >>> from buildkit.config import merge_layers
    >>> defaults = {'db': {'host': 'localhost', 'port': 5432}}
    >>> staging = merge_layers(defaults, {'db': {'host': 'staging-db'}})
    >>> prod = merge_layers(defaults, {'db': {'port': 6432}})
    >>> prod
    {'db': {'host': 'staging-db', 'port': 6432}}    # expected host 'localhost'
    >>> defaults
    {'db': {'host': 'staging-db', 'port': 6432}}    # the defaults changed too

We have also seen edits made to a merged config show up in our defaults afterwards. The module docstring describes the merge contract. Please fix merge_layers() (and load(), which uses it) so it meets that contract; precedence and the list/dict rules must stay as documented.
targetSkill: aliasing and mutation (deep merge without shared state)
